title: Harden full-recrawl postflight health retries and failure propagation
source_ref: ops/ledgers/full-recrawl-closeout-2026-07-31.md; tools/recrawl-health.log shows the July 31 primary full recrawl closed green at 09:59:13 PT and seed refresh closed green at 11:40:05 PT, with no crawl or discovery lock remaining at 14:08 PT. The installed 12:30 launchd window is a retry wake-up and the sync definition uses cadence_seconds=82800 anchored to the 06:00 claim, so no second wrapper start after a green primary run is expected. The July 30 full recrawl recorded completion with api_status=000 api_ok=0. Current tools/recrawl-common.sh finish_wrapper still performs one postflight probe, records completion regardless of api_ok, and returns success. Bounded live proof: health status=ok db=ok, total_sites=4343 avg_score=38, developer=1320, other=850, spam=1.
acceptance_criteria: Preserve the July 31 aggregate closeout and do not start another full recrawl to reproduce the July 30 postflight failure.
Add bounded postflight health retries with logged attempt counts, backoff, final HTTP status, and final api_ok state.
Return nonzero when postflight health remains unhealthy after retries so the installed launchd and sync-state retry path can act.
Run IndexNow only after a healthy postflight and log an explicit skip reason otherwise.
Release the local run lock on success, remote-command failure, postflight failure, interruption, and dry-run paths.
Add fixture tests for immediate success, transient 000 then 200, persistent failure, remote-command failure, exit status, IndexNow gating, and lock release.

Verify the installed recurring path on a later scheduled bounded run records either healthy completion or explicit failed/retry state; preserve the primary-plus-retry wake-up design and do not use a manual broad recrawl as the acceptance test.

title: Make MCP monitor registration consent-aware and redact PII telemetry
source_ref: marketing/mcp-register-monitor-consent-privacy-handoff-2026-07-31.md plus 2026-07-31T21:09Z bounded proof: live /monitor returns 200 while /privacy and /terms remain 404. Source proof still shows register_monitor requires email and domain without a consent field or side-effect annotations, immediately calls models.RegisterMonitor, returns an unsubscribe management token, and stores full arguments in both mcp_requests.arguments and intent_events.metadata.arguments. Fresh redacted aggregates are active=5 and quarantined=3. No crawl lock remains.
acceptance_criteria: Do not register a monitor or use a third-party email while implementing or testing this repair.
Add a pending-confirmation state and one-time confirmation flow; only confirmed rows are eligible for scheduled checks and alerts, while shared-host quarantine remains intact.
Require an explicit consent or inbox-ownership assertion and advertise the email side effect through the MCP tool description and side-effect annotations.

Redact at the shared MCP logging boundary so raw emails, confirmation tokens, and unsubscribe tokens cannot enter mcp_requests.arguments or intent_events.metadata; retain only allowlisted aggregate fields.

Return stable status and confirmation-delivery fields, avoid exposing an unsubscribe token before confirmation, keep duplicates idempotent, and replace raw internal error propagation with bounded public error classes.

Add tests for missing consent, pending registration, confirmation, expired and replayed tokens, duplicates, delivery failure, legacy active rows, quarantine, rate limits, analytics redaction, token non-disclosure, and REST/MCP parity.

After a later product-worker deploy, verify the MCP schema, confirmation delivery, activation, unsubscribe, redacted analytics, REST parity, and monitor-worker eligibility with a Foundry-owned test inbox.

title: Make check_url mutation and telemetry explicit before promotion
source_ref: marketing/mcp-check-url-mutation-contract-handoff-2026-07-31.md plus 2026-07-31T21:09Z bounded proof: live MCP tools/list describes check_url as a verify-before-use check without the submissions-table side effect and returns annotations=null; live GET /api/v1/check documents an on-demand score but not an index refresh. Source inspection shows MCP check_url and REST POST /api/v1/check asynchronously call models.UpsertSite, which rewrites the indexed site record, while the shared MCP boundary logs the full URL argument into mcp_requests.arguments and intent_events.metadata.arguments. Live health, MCP, check docs, llms.txt, OpenAPI, /api/v1, and mcp.json are 200; Agent Card remains 404. Fresh redacted proof has monitor active=5 quarantined=3 and score-fix real-candidate pending=10 with no real paid or lead rows.
acceptance_criteria: Choose and document one parity contract for MCP check_url and REST /api/v1/check: read-only live check or explicitly mutating refresh-and-check.
If read-only, remove UpsertSite and prove a bounded successful check changes neither existing site state nor index membership.

If mutating, add accurate MCP annotations and descriptions, REST/OpenAPI and /api/v1 disclosure, a persistence outcome field, and bounded public error classes; do not report write success before the outcome is known.

Normalize input to scheme plus hostname before logging, reject userinfo, and strip query strings and fragments from both analytics stores; retain only allowlisted aggregate result status and coarse score-band fields.

Add tests for existing and new domains, persistence failure, duplicate checks, timeouts, userinfo, signed query strings, fragments, private-host rejection, analytics redaction, REST/MCP parity, rate limits, and annotation accuracy.

After a later product-worker deploy, verify live tools/list, MCP and REST responses, GET /api/v1/check, /api/v1, /openapi.yaml, /llms.txt, /.well-known/mcp.json, aggregate-only analytics, and the chosen persistence behavior using a Foundry-owned fixture.
Keep register_monitor out of the next-action response until its separate consent, confirmation, token, and telemetry repair is complete.

Do not revive older public check_url conversion drafts until this repair passes and any later external action has identity verification, duplicate-ledger checks, a sync-state public-action lock, and delivery proof.
